Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

# Task 901d0831: repeat local seed motif across 3x3 tiles

A grid is segmented into equal rectangular panels by full separator rows and columns (separator color 4 in examples). Each panel is 3x3 in observed cases. One panel contains a small pattern of non-background cells (background 1); copy that 3x3 motif into every panel, preserving the separators. Do not repeat the seed motif identically row-for-row: retain each cell's relative coordinate and color.

## Demonstration
Input 11x5, separator column 2 and rows 3,7 (zero-based), background 1. Seed pattern occupies the upper-left 3x2 panel: row0 `[6,6]`, row1 `[8,1]`, row2 `[1,1]`. Output repeats this motif across the right panel and then repeats the three-row tile vertically, with separator rows/column unchanged:
rows motif pattern `[6,6,2,6,6]`, `[8,1,2,8,1]`, `[1,1,2,1,1]`, repeated, with all-2 separator rows. This indicates tiled motif replication across all panels, matching non-background seed cells; background remains background.

## Additional confirmation: task stream recurrence
A 13x15 test used background 7 and separator color 6: full separator column at zero-based column 7 and full separator row at row 6. The upper-left 6x7 panel contained the motif; output copied its local coordinates and exact colors into the upper-right 6x7 panel and both lower panels (the same local rows/columns), preserving separator lines. The motif in this case is all non-background 5s from the upper-left panel; every background 7 stays 7. The panel dimensions need not be 3x3: copy the pattern of non-background cells at matching local offsets across the separator-defined panels, using actual grid dimensions.

## Test evidence: 17x29 with 3x9 panels
A test grid had separator rows at 8 and separator columns at 9 and 19 (zero-based), yielding six 8x9 panels. Background was 1 and separator color 3. The seed motif was in the upper-left panel: 7 at local (0,0), 9 at (0,1), 7 at (2,2), and 0 at (3,5). Replicating those exact colored coordinates into all six panels while preserving background and separators was accepted. This confirms the rule applies to panels larger than 3x3; copy only the sparse non-background markers at the same local coordinates.

## Test and recovery evidence
Test 17x11, separators color 4 at columns 3,7 and rows 5,11. Panels are 3x3. Seed motif in panel row-block 1, col-block 0 (zero-based):
`[[1,1,7],[9,1,1],[1,7,1]]`.
Copy that 3x3 pattern to every 3x3 panel, preserve separators. Correct output was confirmed after two wrong submissions.

Important: initial incorrect attempt used an incorrect 3x3 periodic motif phase; second incorrect attempt placed motif rows cyclically shifted. Correct motif alignment is exact: seed's local row/column coordinates map directly to the same local coordinates in every panel. The successful grid repeats the motif in all 3x3 panels, leaves background 1 cells unchanged, and keeps all separator lines 4.

## Additional confirmation: 13x23 test with 6x7 panels
A test used background 3 and separator color 8, with one full separator row at zero-based row 6 and separator columns at zero-based columns 7 and 15. The upper-left 6x7 panel contained color-2 markers at local coordinates `(0,3)`, `(0,5)`, `(2,1)`, `(2,5)`, `(2,6)`, `(3,2)`, `(3,3)`. Copy these exact marker coordinates into every 6x7 panel (2 panel rows x 3 panel columns), preserving all background 3 cells and separator 8 lines. This was accepted with zero wrong submissions. It reinforces exact local-offset replication even when the motif is sparse and asymmetric.

## Critical correction from a failed instance (11x15 test)

Prior tile replication interpretations repeatedly failed on this input, including attempted 3x3/6x7-style motif copying. Do not tile the input's sparse contents by default: separator lines can instead partition a grid into unrelated panels whose rules may be different.

Evidence from two demos in this occurrence:
- Demo 1: 13x9, full horizontal separator row r6 of color5. Top 6x9 region is copied exactly to rows7-12; all-background bottom region is not preserved as background. Output repeats the entire top 6-row region verbatim below separator. No vertical separators in this example.
- Demo 2: 3x13, full vertical separator column c6 of color3. The left panel c0-5, initially mostly background2 with a vertical sequence at c2 in rows0-2 = [2,2,2], is transformed so that c2 becomes [8,0,7] in rows0-2 and c0 becomes [2,2,7], c1 remains2, c3 becomes [2,2,9]. This exactly copies the *rightmost three columns* (c10-12 = [[2,2,2],[2,2,2],[2,2,2]]? Wait input's visible non-background triplet is c9=8,0,9 and c7=2,2,7; output left c0-5 encodes a rearranged 3x3 pattern [8,0,7; 2,2,2; 7,9,...] and is not adequately explained by the old generic tiling hypothesis. Preserve separator and right panel unchanged. Rule unresolved; seek additional demo(s) and derive panel-specific transform from exact coordinates before submitting.
